T: Feed Meeko first. He won't wait.
D: A young woman in 1607 Virginia meets an English settler and tries to keep the peace.
P: Serve the snacks when Meeko goes digging through John Smith's bag for biscuits.
S: Meeko the raccoon raiding the biscuits
Buttermilk biscuits of flour, cold butter and buttermilk, cut into rounds and baked at 220C for 14 minutes, split with butter and honey.
the river that runs around the bend
Corn kernels mixed with flour, egg, spring onion and chilli, fried in spoonfuls until golden, with a lime and sour cream dip.
Grandmother Willow, the wise old tree
Pecans, walnuts and pepitas roasted with maple syrup and a pinch of salt at 170C for 12 minutes, cooled into clusters.
M: the Virginia harvest of corn, beans and squash
Chicken thighs simmered with pumpkin, corn, kidney beans, tomato and smoked paprika until thick, served with cornbread.
the English settlers building their fort
Beef and onion pie of chuck simmered 2 hours in stock and ale, under a puff pastry lid baked at 200C for 25 minutes.
W: the colours of the wind in autumn
Peaches halved and roasted at 200C with maple syrup and butter for 15 minutes, with vanilla ice cream and crushed pecans.
K: the forest berries and the river
Cranberry juice and sparkling water with fresh blueberries and mint over ice.

s.note: Meeko the raccoon raiding the biscuits
s.how: Rub 100g cold butter into 450g self-raising flour with a pinch of salt. Stir in 300ml buttermilk until it just comes together. Pat out, cut into rounds and bake at 220C for 14 minutes until tall and golden. Split while warm and spread with butter and honey.

s.note: Grandmother Willow, the wise old tree
s.how: Toss 100g pecans, 100g walnuts and 50g pepitas with 4 tbsp maple syrup and a pinch of sea salt. Spread on a lined tray and roast at 170C for 12 minutes, stirring once. Leave to cool completely so they set, then break into rough clusters.

m.note: the Virginia harvest of corn, beans and squash
m.how: Brown 600g diced chicken thighs, then add 500g diced butternut pumpkin, a can of corn, a can of drained kidney beans, a can of crushed tomatoes and a teaspoon of smoked paprika. Simmer 40 minutes until thick. Bake a quick cornbread from cornmeal, flour, egg and milk to serve alongside.

w.note: the colours of the wind in autumn
w.how: Halve 4 ripe peaches and remove the stones. Sit cut side up in a baking dish, dot with butter and drizzle with maple syrup. Roast at 200C for 15 minutes until soft and syrupy. Serve warm with a scoop of vanilla ice cream and crushed pecans on top.

d.note: the forest berries and the river
d.how: Fill tall glasses with ice, a few fresh blueberries and a couple of mint leaves. Pour in cranberry juice to halfway, then top with cold sparkling water. Stir gently so the berries swirl like a river current and serve straight away.
